text:
**A 200-watt panel refills a 1,000Wh station in about a day and a half of decent sun. A 300-400W panel does it in about one day.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Panel watts to refill 1,000Wh from empty in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

- **Winter:** Held in Reserve estimates about 735W for a northern January, with 2 peak sun hours ([source](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **If you can wait longer:** A 200W panel gives roughly 600-630Wh per day at 4-4.5 peak sun hours, so it takes about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)). A 100W panel takes about 3 days.
- **Quick rule of thumb:** Divide the watt-hours by 5 to get the panel size that refills in about 1.5 days, so 1,000Wh needs about 200W ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Check these before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps the watts it accepts. A 200W limit means a 400W array adds nothing at midday, though extra panel can help in weak light ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay under the station's maximum input voltage. Going over can damage the charge controller, and panels wired in series add their voltages.
- **Running loads:** If you use the station while it charges, subtract that draw from the solar input, and the recharge takes longer.

**One option if you want the one-day recharge:** The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) has a 45.3V Voc, which fits 12-60V solar inputs, and comes with MC4→XT60 and DC adapters. As of 2026-10-21 it was $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (the page says the code expires 2026-12-30). It weighs 18.5 kg, which is heavy for a folding panel, and it's too high-voltage for stations with low input windows, such as 5-24V or 12-28V models. That page is an affiliate listing, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through it. If your station only accepts 200W, a 200W panel is the better value.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its solar input limit and suggest a matching panel.
